data.title: Disclosure of sensitive data in URL parameters
data.summary:
The web application sent sensitive data as URL parameters in HTTP requests. 
Data sent as URL parameters is stored in the browser cache and can potentially appear in various other places such as web server logs, referer headers or shared systems. 
Third parties could thus gain access to this sensitive data.
data.description:
The application sends sensitive data in the URL parameter `<PARAMETER_NAME>` at `<URL>`. The request below transmits `<SENSITIVE_DATA>` in the query string:

```http
GET <URL>?<PARAMETER_NAME>=<VALUE> HTTP/1.1
Host: <HOST>
```

URLs are not treated as confidential. Browsers store them in history, proxies and web servers write them to access logs, and the browser sends them in the `Referer` header when the user follows a link to another site or the page loads external resources. Anyone with access to one of these locations can read the value.

This could expose the data in the following places:
* Referer Header
* Web Logs
* Shared Systems
* Browser History
* Browser Cache
* Shoulder Surfing
data.recommendation:
* The application should send all sensitive data in the body of an HTTP message, e.g. in the body of a POST request.
* Protect the transmission with HTTPS.
data.short_recommendation: To protect sensitive data from access by third parties, it should be sent in the body of an HTTP message, e.g. via POST request.
